keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Infobox 'Dates 700-150 BCE'; 'They lived in northern Hebei, southeastern Inner Mongolia and the western part of Liaoning ... along the Yan Mountains and Greater Khingan Range'. The dossier starts at the first dated event, 300 BCE (Qin Kai); the infobox's earlier centuries have no event or extent on the page. The page gives no area. Revised after review: the shape no longer draws Cliopatria's Yan of 291 (139 grid cells, about 35,000 km2, 16 percent of the earlier shape, mostly Liaoxi), the land Yan holds after Qin Kai's campaign of 300 BCE (yan ledger 6 gains it 'from Donghu'); the Donghu page names no land taken, so the cut is Cliopatria's Yan and the researcher's reading.

region.text: northern Hebei, south-eastern Inner Mongolia and the western part of Liaoning, along the Yan Mountains and the Greater Khingan Range, without the land Yan already held in 292

ledger.note: 300 BCE: the Donghu are the neighbours of Yan. 'In 300 BCE Qin Kai, a general taken hostage from the state of Yan ... defeated the Donghu after having gained the esteem of the Donghu.' The infobox starts the Donghu in 700 BCE; the first dated sentence is used. The page gives no boundary and no transfer of land to Yan; the region leaves out Cliopatria's Yan of 292 (70 grid cells of the circles below lay inside it) and the loss to Yan follows in the same year.

region.text: Cliopatria's Yan growth of 291 outside the Liaodong region: the lands of the Donghu taken by Qin Kai's campaign (yan ledger 6)

ledger.note: 300 BCE: Yan's frontier advances against the Donghu. 'In 300 BCE Qin Kai, a general taken hostage from the state of Yan ... defeated the Donghu after having gained the esteem of the Donghu and learning their battle tactics' (Donghu people page, which says nothing about land taken). The year is the page's; the land (the 76 cells of Cliopatria's Yan growth of 291 outside the Liaodong region, 69 of them inside the circles that make up this dossier's region) is the researcher's reading, mirroring yan ledger 6 (gain, counterpart 'Donghu', confidence 2).

region.text: northern Hebei, south-eastern Inner Mongolia and the western part of Liaoning, along the Yan Mountains and the Greater Khingan Range, without the land Yan holds after Qin Kai's campaign (Cliopatria's Yan of 291)

ledger.note: 208 BCE: Modu destroys the Donghu. 'By 208 BCE, the Donghu had been defeated and their remnants split into the Xianbei and Wuhuan tribes'; 'When their eastern neighbors, the Donghu, expressed desire to occupy uninhabited land between them, Modu reacted by attacking them.' The Donghu page's lead has them 'taken over by the Xiongnu in 150 BCE' (infobox end), which the dossier does not follow.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Donghu; ia-01-a asked for a dossier -300..-208). The xiongnu dossier's loss event draws the Donghu land as eastern Mongolia and Manchuria from the Xiongnu page; this dossier follows the Donghu page (northern Hebei, south-east Inner Mongolia, west Liaoning), so a gap-filler should reconcile the two regions (the Xiongnu page's eastern border at the Liao River suggests the Donghu lay mostly west of it). The Donghu page's lead and infobox give 150 BCE for the Xiongnu take-over, 358 years after the earliest date in the infobox and 58 years after the Modu Chanyu page's 208 BCE; the dossier follows the latter. Revised after review (ia-01-x fix pass): the yan dossier gains 'the lands of the Donghu' in 300 BCE (ledger 6, Cliopatria's Yan growth of 291 outside Liaodong), so this dossier now records the mirror loss to 'yan' (ledger 1) and draws the Donghu without Cliopatria's Yan of 291 (keyframe, dissolve and the Xiongnu war zone), which removes the Liaoxi double-draw; the yan owner should use the slug donghu in place of the string 'Donghu'. The loss region is a reading, because the page says only that Qin Kai 'defeated the Donghu'. Open page, re-read: the Donghu 'lived in northern Hebei, southeastern Inner Mongolia and the western part of Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang' (Jilin and Heilongjiang are not drawn). Wuhuan needs a dossier (flagged to ea-02/ea-03). No capital or ruler is recorded; no area. Gazetteer names used (Liaoxi, Chifeng, Chengde) resolve.
